target.name: Foundation Robotics
target.founder: Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, Mike LeBlanc

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Foundation Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, and Mike LeBlanc. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of nine private robotics companies and one public comparable, spanning seed through Series B stages, with the most relevant peers including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $50M in reported total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, implying $100M. The peer-median method anchors to four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B and a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. These peers—Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed)—reflect recent market pricing in the robotics sector.

The triangulation supports a range of $85M to $2.0B, with a median implied valuation of $900M. The wide dispersion reflects substantial uncertainty inherent in early-stage valuation: stage-progression analysis suggests early-cycle value while peer comparables suggest the market has priced later-stage robotics companies substantially higher. Key sensitivities include Foundation Robotics' progress toward Series B funding, customer traction relative to listed peers, and sector-wide valuation momentum.
